“Economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace” is clearly positive on growth, but the Financial Stability Report reflecting conditions as of April 11, 2025 points to ongoing vulnerabilities—commercial real estate exposures, run-prone short‑term funding in parts of the nonbank sector (prime and offshore dollar MMFs), sizable risk‑asset mutual fund AUM (high‑yield and bank‑loan funds), and episodic strains in Treasury market liquidity. Coupled with still‑somewhat‑elevated inflation and a restrictive policy stance (4.25–4.50% target range, continued balance‑sheet runoff), the tone should be marked as positive but deliberately cautious rather than strongly upbeat.
